messages:
Julie: FYI - AcmeLabs (org 98765) opened a ticket: they hit monthly quota at the cycle boundary and got 429s after console showed the refill. Tossing details here so we can triage.

James (AcmeLabs): I ran a burst at ~2024-05-03T23:55 PDT and burned the remainder. Console shows quota back at 2024-05-04T00:00:00Z but my requests were 429ing until ~00:07. Sample: 

`curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\"`
Response: 429 {\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\",\"message\":\"monthly quota exhausted\",\"retry_after\":0}
Request-ID: req_20240504_abc123

Raj: Can you confirm org_id, plan (hosted/dedicated), and billing window? Also, do you have any mirroring/edge tokens?

Julie: Org 98765, hosted tier, monthly 250k tokens. No dedicated. Heavy burst ended ~23:58 PDT.

billing-bot: refill-job started for org 98765 job_id=refill_20240504_9921
billing-bot: refill-job finished job_id=refill_20240504_9921 status=ok tokens_added=250000 propagated_event_id=evt_55e7

Janet (ops): Tailing token-service and edge-proxy. Refill event emitted at 2024-05-04T00:00:02Z (evt_55e7). Token-service acknowledged at 00:00:03Z. Noting default edge prefix cache TTL=300s; if an edge node had stale cache state it could keep answering as exhausted until TTL/invalidations clear.

Kevin: We push an invalidation event but the edge proxies subscribe asynchronously. In rare paths (concurrent Redis timeouts/failover) invalidation can be delayed until TTL. I just spotted a Redis timeout at 2024-05-04T00:01:18Z which may have impacted fan-out for a subset of workers. So refill itself succeeded; propagation lag + cache TTL explains the ~6m 429 window.

Julie: Customer wants an immediate mitigation - they lost traffic during a promo. What can support offer right now?

Kevin: Two practical options: 
1) Manual top-up from support/admin UI (instant). Use admin flow to credit tokens and note reason = "manual recovery - propagation lag".
2) Recommend retry (backoff) — requests typically succeed within a few minutes once all edges see the invalidation. Ask customer to include request-ids so we can trace failed attempts.

Kevin: Internal admin snippet (for support ops only):
```
POST https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/orgs/98765/topup
Headers: X-Admin-Token: <redacted>
Body: {"tokens":250000, "reason":"manual recovery - propagation lag"}
```

Janet (ops): Quick health check: small chance of delayed invalidation if refill coincides with Redis failover, forcing retries in the invalidation fan-out. Filed ENG ticket ENG-11234 to add a synchronous fallback for small refills and to harden fan-out error handling.

Raj: Short customer-facing blurb: "Your account was refilled at the start of your billing cycle. We use distributed caching at our API edge to optimize latency; occasionally there can be a short propagation delay (usually under 10 minutes) during which some requests may still see the previous exhausted state. If you see 429s after your cycle boundary, please retry after a minute and include the request-id in a support reply; we can also apply a manual top-up immediately while we investigate." Keep it concise.

Julie: Sent that to the customer. They asked if this is DST/timezone-related.

Kevin: Clarified: not a timezone bug. Refill scheduling is anchored to the billing boundary in UTC by policy; the visible mismatch here is propagation/invalidation lag, not the scheduled refill time.

James (AcmeLabs): We retried at ~00:07 UTC and calls started succeeding. Thanks for the clarification — will reach back if it happens again.

Julie: Closing ticket and attaching logs/request-ids. Follow-ups: ops add runbook step for on-call/support to perform manual top-ups (doc: support/runbooks/topup-manual); ENG to track ENG-11234 for synchronous fallback.

Janet (ops): Metrics note: similar propagation anomalies appear in <0.1% of refills over 90d. Adding to ops triage board and flagging for monitoring alerts on fan-out retry rate.

Kevin: If anyone needs raw logs/req ids ping me and I'll paste lanes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
